html:
The Marinahua are a small Panoan-speaking people of the upper Purus basin in southeastern Peru, near the border with Brazil. They are closely related to the Sharanahua and the Chitonahua, and their language is close to theirs.

Like many peoples of the region, they were scattered by the rubber boom, which brought slave raids and disease. Most Marinahua now live in mixed villages with Sharanahua along the Purus and its tributaries, and they are counted with them in most surveys.
